proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance

proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
proposals.source: Vehicle IMU and tracker yaw-rate noise figures.

proposals.name: p.caravan_entry_time_headway
proposals.convention: Minimum accepted lead and lag time gap of a merging or lane-changing vehicle, applied once ahead of and once behind the entering vehicle.
proposals.source: Lane-change gap-acceptance studies (critical lead and lag gaps of about one second).

proposals.name: p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length
proposals.convention: Overall length of the longest design combination a highway is designed for (an interstate semitrailer combination), so that any vehicle or combination can occupy the space.
proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, WB-67 design vehicle overall length.

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

proposals.name: p.same_direction_cos_tolerance
proposals.convention: Heading alignment: cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same way of travel (about a quarter of a right angle), covering lane changes and road bends.
proposals.source: Lane-change trajectory geometry in naturalistic driving data.

proposals.name: p.straight_through_max_heading_change
proposals.convention: Turning-movement classification at a junction: a crossing whose net heading change stays below this bound is a through movement, not a turn.
proposals.source: Intersection turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

proposals.name: p.against_direction_cos_tolerance
proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which a heading still points against a carrier's designated direction (about half a right angle).
proposals.source: Wrong-way-driving detection practice (heading opposed to the lane direction beyond a cone).

proposals.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change to the left beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

proposals.name: p.reversal_max_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude beyond which the heading has come round past the opposite direction (a loop rather than a reversal).
proposals.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

proposals.name: p.reversal_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal); also the upper end of a left turn's band.
proposals.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window
proposals.convention: The time within which a turn or a reversal, a reversal made in several moves included, is completed: the window over which the heading change that recognizes it is measured.
proposals.source: Intersection turning times and three-point-turn durations in naturalistic driving data.

proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
proposals.source: Vehicle IMU and tracker yaw-rate noise figures.

proposals.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
proposals.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.

proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance

proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon

proposals.convention: The heading change to the right beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift; the right-hand counterpart of the left-turn bound.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide turning-movement counts; the left-turn bound of this reading).

proposals.name: p.straight_through_max_heading_change
proposals.convention: Turning-movement classification at a junction: a crossing whose net heading change stays below this bound is a through movement.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change to the left beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.reversal_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal); also the upper bound of a turn.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.right_turn_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change to the right beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift; the right-hand counterpart of the left-turn bound.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide turning-movement counts; the left-turn bound of this reading).

proposals.name: p.straight_through_max_heading_change
proposals.convention: Turning-movement classification at a junction: a crossing whose net heading change stays below this bound is a through movement.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

proposals.name: p.reversal_max_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude beyond which the heading has come round past the opposite direction (a loop rather than a reversal).
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.reversal_min_angle
proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal); also the upper bound of a turn.
proposals.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide).

proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window
proposals.convention: The time within which a turn or a reversal, a reversal made in several moves included, is completed: the window over which the heading change is recognized.
proposals.source: Observed durations of U-turns and multi-point turns.

proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
proposals.source: Yaw-rate noise of tracked vehicles.

proposals.name: p.course_change_sin_tolerance
proposals.convention: Lane-change kinematics: the heading of a vehicle changing lanes or turning departs from the lane direction by about three degrees or more, a smaller departure being in-lane steering correction; the bound is the sine of that angle.
proposals.source: Naturalistic lane-change trajectory studies (heading-angle distributions of lane changes, e.g. Toledo and Zohar 2007; NGSIM lane-change analyses).

proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

proposals.name: p.off_roadway_reach
proposals.convention: One standard lane width (12 ft): a shoulder separated from the vehicle's body by no more than one lane is reachable by one lateral move, and is beside the vehicle.
proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (standard 12 ft travel lane).

proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

proposals.name: p.free_passage_width
proposals.convention: Width a passing design vehicle needs: the 8.5 ft (2.6 m) design vehicle width plus a shy margin of about 0.4 m.
proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (design vehicle dimensions).

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about the sum of two passenger-car half-lengths.
proposals.source: Design passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
proposals.source: Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987), time-to-collision thresholds

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it.
proposals.source: Car-following models' standstill (jam) distance, e.g. the Intelligent Driver Model and Wiedemann

proposals.name: p.following_min_time_headway
proposals.convention: Car-following: the smallest time gap to the road user ahead at which a following driver can still react to its braking; gaps below it are classed as close following.
proposals.source: Time-headway criteria of naturalistic driving and traffic-flow studies

proposals.name: p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed
proposals.convention: Time-to-line-crossing convention: drifting at a heading error of about one degree, a vehicle keeps at least one second before its body reaches the lane edge, so the free lateral margin it needs is its speed times the sine of that error times that time.
proposals.source: Godthelp, Milgram and Blaauw (1984), time-to-line-crossing

proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.
proposals.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance

proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_dry
proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.
proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate

proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow
proposals.convention: Deceleration an icy or snow-covered surface sustains: a friction coefficient of about a tenth, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
proposals.source: Winter road friction measurements (PIARC Snow and Ice Databook)

proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_wet
proposals.convention: Deceleration a wet paved surface sustains: a wet-pavement friction coefficient of about a quarter at highway speeds, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
proposals.source: Pavement skid-resistance data (AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction)

proposals.source: Geometric convention for opposing-direction classification (headings within a half right angle of opposed)
